title: Entitlement lifecycle: feature-flag pricing experiments for observability retention + compliance pack
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal:
Run a set of controlled experiments that determine the optimal bundling, pricing, and gating mechanics for two enterprise add-ons: extended observability retention and a compliance/security questionnaire + advisory pack. We want to identify which packaging approaches trade off conversion lift vs revenue per account, while minimizing friction for sales/legal and enabling clean contract language for enterprise deals.

Hypotheses:
1) A tiered retention add-on priced as per-route retention credits will convert more self-serve teams than a flat monthly add-on because it aligns cost to traffic patterns.
2) Packaging compliance questionnaire support (template answers + one review session) as a seat-based SKU will increase deal velocity for regulated customers if surfaced during onboarding and available as a per-deal entitlement in contracts.
3) Offering a bundled "observability + compliance" discount (10–15%) will increase average deal size without materially increasing churn if we attach a 12-month minimum commitment.

Experiment matrix (cohorts):
- Control: current catalog (no change).
- C1: Retention-only: per-route retention credits (monthly buckets) behind feature flag; UI + API pricing visible.
- C2: Compliance-only: seat-based compliance pack (includes questionnaire answers + 2h review).
- C3: Bundle-flat: both add-ons as a single monthly bundle with 10% discount.
- C4: Bundle-metered: both add-ons sold separately but cross-sell suggestions + 15% bundle credit applied at invoice if both purchased.

Pricing knobs to evaluate:
- Retention: flat addon vs per-GB vs per-route monthly credits.
- Compliance: per-seat vs per-contract fee vs included in Dedicated/Private tiers.
- Discounts: percentage vs fixed credits; minimum-term requirement (monthly vs 12-month).

Contract & Security considerations:
- Need a contract amendment template with clear entitlement lines for retention buckets and compliance seats. Legal must approve wording that maps retention credits to billing metric.
- Security team must sign off on what "compliance pack" delivers (templates only vs advisory) so we can represent it in the Security Questionnaire and SLAs.
- KMS/HSM or on-prem customers may need a different mapping; add a checkbox in the questionnaire to route to Solutions Eng for bespoke pricing.

Success metrics (signal + guardrails):
- Primary: conversion rate lift for paid plans in pilot cohorts (target +8% over control) and MRR delta per cohort.
- Secondary: average deal size, time-to-sign for enterprise deals flagged as regulated, cross-sell rate.
- Operational: accuracy of billing events for retention credits (error rate <0.1%), no increase in support ticket volume >20% during rollout.
- Safety guardrail: no SLO regressions caused by retention changes (latency/throughput targets unchanged).

Telemetry & dashboards required:
- Cohort enrollment dashboard (by account tier, region, route patterns).
- Conversion funnel for each cohort (trial -> paid -> addon purchase).
- Billing reconciliation: expected vs invoiced retention credits.
- Support ticket heatmap (questions about pricing/entitlement).

Implementation plan:
1) PM: finalize pricing knobs and experiment definitions; draft customer-facing copy for Console and billing pages.
2) Design: mockups for addon purchase flow, enterprise checkout, and contract clause snippets.
3) Engineering: feature flags, API fields for retention credits, telemetry events, billing connector changes (invoice line items). Engineering spike to estimate effort.
4) Legal/Security: draft contract amendment language and Security Questionnaire mapping; define delivery SLAs for the compliance pack.
5) Sales pilot: recruit 8–12 enterprise customers (mix of Dedicated and Hosted) for an opt-in pilot; select 400 trial accounts for self-serve cohorts.
6) Experiment duration: 8 weeks per cohort; interim review at 4 weeks.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Billing complexity causes invoice disputes. Mitigation: run a 2-week dry-run billing report (no invoice changes) and validate with Finance.
- Risk: Customers expect a higher level of advisory with compliance pack. Mitigation: clearly document deliverables and limit advisory hours; route out-of-scope requests to SES with T&M.
- Risk: Feature-flag drift causing inconsistent UX. Mitigation: tie flags to account-level entitlement and use strict rollout checklist.
